subject: Unexpected February usage surge — request for clarification and logs
messages:
From: Tom Burke <tburke@deltasoft.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: accounts-payable@deltasoft.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected spike on February invoice — request for explanation

Hi Vanessa,

We received the February invoice and there's a ~3x increase in billable tokens compared to January. This is out of line with our usage patterns — we didn't change traffic or onboarding volume on our side. Can you help explain what drove this surge and provide a token-level export for Feb? AP is holding payment until we understand the variance; they'd like a line-item breakdown we can attach to the PO.

Key details: our plan monthly commitment is 1M tokens; February invoice shows 3.2M billable tokens and a large overage charge. Please confirm whether the billing aggregation window or a recent tokenizer change could have affected counts.

Thanks,
Tom Burke
Head of Platform
Deltasoft

--
Tom Burke
Deltasoft
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Tom Burke <tburke@deltasoft.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, accounts-payable@deltasoft.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on February invoice — request for explanation

Hi Tom — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the stress. We're pulling the Feb usage export now and will include token-level breakdowns by endpoint and by day. A few quick questions to help narrow scope:

- Did you run any backfill, replay, or bulk embedding jobs in Feb? Those are a common cause of sudden spikes.
- Are you using any customer-side batching that might have re-run after an error?

I'll loop in our billing lead (Marissa) to track credits if appropriate. We're going to: 1) export hourly token logs for Feb, 2) check for duplicate request IDs and aggregation-window overlaps, 3) validate tokenizer/runtime version used for those calls. We'll share a CSV and a one-page summary within two business days.

If you prefer a quick call to walk through the export, I'm available tomorrow 11:00–12:00 PST.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123

Attachment: (none yet)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Deltasoft Feb spike — prepare export & credit guidance

Vanessa — noted. Quick internal plan:

1) I'll pull the billing ledger and calculate the dollar impact (estimate right now: ~$1,200 overage).
2) Infra: can you run the token-export job scoped to Deltasoft tenant id for 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28 and include request_id, endpoint, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, timestamp? We need to confirm whether counts were doubled by a replay or if an aggregation cutoff produced overlapping windows.
3) Policy: for first-time unexpected surges where a customer has not intentionally increased traffic, we can offer a one-time goodwill credit up to 50% of the overage while we investigate. I'll hold off finalizing the credit until we review the raw logs.

Sean — tagging you for any routing/aggregation anomalies you've seen in infra (especially anything around the Feb 8–10 batch window).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Tom Burke <tburke@deltasoft.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, accounts-payable@deltasoft.com
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 15:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on February invoice — results and one-time credit

Hi Tom — thanks for your patience. We've completed our analysis and attached the token-level export (usage_export_202602.csv) plus a PDF summary of billing line items. Short summary up front:

- Root cause: a backfill job run by your team on Feb 9 reprocessed ~900k requests that had already been handled earlier in the month. The job included both generation and embedding calls; combined with our aggregation window behavior some requests were re-counted across two windows because the replay's timestamps straddled a midnight cutoff. Infra confirmed no tokenizer regression on Redwood's side.

- Impact: total billable tokens for February increased to 3,210,482. Of that, ~950k tokens are attributable to the replay/backfill.

- Resolution & next steps: we are applying a one-time credit for 60% of the replay-attributable overage (credit amount: $1,140) as a goodwill adjustment given this is the first incident. The credit will appear on your March invoice. Attached: usage_export_202602.csv (token-level rows) and billing_line_items_Feb2026.pdf (human-readable invoice lines).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute post-mortem to walk through the export and share recommendations to avoid double-counting (e.g., idempotent request IDs, stricter cutoff windows for backfills, or using batch-only endpoints).

Thanks again — please let me know if AP needs any different formatting for the CSV for PO reconciliation.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123

Attachments: usage_export_202602.csv (CSV, 1.2MB stub), billing_line_items_Feb2026.pdf (PDF, 320KB stub)
